title: Unique Buttery Indian Milk Kheer
description: A creamy and buttery Indian kheer made with wholegrain bread and slow-cooked to perfection, featuring the distinct flavors of Chettinad cuisine, this dish is FODMAP-friendly and easy to make on a weeknight.
instructions: Begin by tearing the wholegrain bread into small pieces and soaking them in milk for at least 30 minutes.
In a large saucepan, melt the unsalted butter over medium heat.
Add the cardamom powder and saffron threads to the melted butter and stir well.
Remove the bread pieces from the milk, squeezing out as much milk as possible, and add them to the saucepan.
Cook the bread mixture for about 10 minutes, stirring frequently, until it is lightly toasted and fragrant.
Add the milk, rose water, almonds, and pistachios to the saucepan and stir well to combine.
Bring the mixture to a simmer and cook for 15-20 minutes, stirring occasionally, until the kheer has thickened and the flavors have melded together.
Remove the saucepan from the heat and let the kheer cool to room temperature.
Serve the Unique Buttery Indian Milk Kheer chilled, garnished with additional almonds and pistachios if desired.
